newsitem.title: UK: Latin American drug market grew 8 pct in 1996 - IMS.
newsitem.headline: Latin American drug market grew 8 pct in 1996 - IMS.

text.p: Latin American drug sales incrased by eight percent in dollar terms in 1996, market researcher IMS International said on Monday.
Sales in Brazil, Latin America's biggest pharmacy market, climbed 15 percent to $7.251 billion, primarily driven by price increases as volumes only rose moderately, IMS said.
Argentina, the continent's second biggest market, was stable with only one percent sales growth to $3.643 billion.
Improved prices also helped Mexican sales, which saw an increase of 14 percent to $2.736 billion.
In sharp contrast, the market in Venezuela shrunk by 20 percent to $503 million because of considerable price falls, while volumes stayed flat.
IMS said its Pharma Strategy Group expects the total Latin American drug market to grow by a compound 11 percent per year during the period from 1997 to 2001.
Brazil and Mexico will be the main drivers as their economies expand and the environment for the pharmaceutical industry improves, IMS said.
